system_description.narrative_title: Iran-Houthi escalation threatens regional war and energy disruption
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative links Iran's backing and precision-strike capabilities with Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, producing a cascade of military posturing, sanctions, diplomatic postponements and disruptions to oil, aviation and regional stability. Treated as an open system, the situation involves flows of materiel, intelligence and strikes between state and proxy actors, feedback loops where attacks provoke sanctions and military planning that in turn raise risks of wider escalation, and nonlinear thresholds (major energy shocks, coalition entry, or direct US–Iran clashes) that could rapidly change system behaviour.
system_description.scope: Actors (Iran, Houthis, Saudi Arabia, US, Gulf states, EU, Israel), geographic focus (Red Sea, Gulf, Arabian Peninsula), processes (proxy strikes, precision targeting, sanctions, military planning, diplomatic engagement/withdrawal), and affected sectors (oil & gas, aviation, regional trade, humanitarian conditions in Yemen).
system_description.super_system: International security and global energy system (global order, markets and strategic military balances)
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil & gas markets and supply chains
International diplomacy and alliance networks (US, EU, GCC)
Commercial aviation and maritime trade security
Humanitarian and food-security situation in Yemen
evidence_headlines: Iran says it’s ‘counting the moments’ until it can strike U.S. warships; Saudi Aramco facilities attacked
How are Yemen’s Houthis attacking Saudi Arabia so effectively?
US issues fresh Iran-related sanctions, Treasury website shows
Houthis attack presidential palace complex in Yemen's Aden, PM unharmed, officials say
EU and Gulf states postpone summit due in Saudi Arabia

variables.name: Precision strike capability
variables.description: Measures the accuracy, range and lethality of long‑range strike systems available in the theatre.

variables.name: Proxy force capacity
variables.description: Measures the manpower, weapons stocks and operational readiness of non‑state or proxy fighting formations.

variables.name: Materiel and intelligence flows
variables.description: Measures the rate and volume of weapons, munitions, fuel and intelligence transfers between principal actors and their proxies.

variables.name: Attack frequency and intensity
variables.description: Measures the tempo and average destructive intensity of hostile strikes against military and civilian targets.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure vulnerability
variables.description: Measures the susceptibility of energy, transport and communication infrastructure to disruption or damage from attacks.

variables.name: Military posturing and readiness
variables.description: Measures force deployments, alert levels and operational planning intensity among armed actors in the region.

variables.name: Sanctions and economic restrictions
variables.description: Measures the breadth and strictness of trade, financial and economic measures applied against actors in the conflict system.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement and mediation
variables.description: Measures the frequency and scale of diplomatic contacts, negotiations and mediation efforts aimed at de‑escalation.

variables.name: Energy supply flow
variables.description: Measures the physical volumetric flow of oil and gas through regional export routes and chokepoints into global markets.

variables.name: Transport and aviation disruption
variables.description: Measures the rate and extent of interruptions to maritime shipping lanes, airports and commercial aviation services.

variables.name: Insurance and risk premia
variables.description: Measures the additional insurance costs and risk‑related surcharges applied to shipping, energy shipments and regional commerce.

variables.name: Energy market volatility
variables.description: Measures short‑term price volatility and market sensitivity in energy commodities tied to geopolitical disruptions.

variables.name: Humanitarian crisis severity
variables.description: Measures levels of displacement, civilian casualties and essential‑needs shortfalls among affected populations.

variables.name: Proximity to escalation thresholds
variables.description: Measures how close the system is to nonlinear escalation triggers such as major energy shocks, coalition entry or direct inter‑state clashes.

variables.name: Strike attribution clarity
variables.description: Measures the degree of certainty in identifying perpetrators of attacks and linking actions to sponsoring actors.

variables.name: Coalition cohesion and coordination
variables.description: Measures the degree of alignment, information‑sharing and coordinated action among responding actors and partnerships.

catalysts.title: Iran increases targeting and intelligence support to Houthis
catalysts.description: Ongoing transfer of targeting data, battle plans and guidance from Iran to Houthi forces, raising their operational effectiveness. Likely to continue as recent reporting documents direct assistance.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran Is Giving Houthis Targeting and Intelligence' and related reporting on Houthi effectiveness.

catalysts.title: Houthis sustain attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities
catalysts.description: Continuing Houthi campaign targeting aviation and energy infrastructure, including strikes on airports and Aramco sites, with operational pledges to continue attacks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities'; 'Saudi Aramco headquarters suffered extensive damage.'

catalysts.title: U.S. deliberation over large-scale strikes on Iran
catalysts.description: Active consideration within U.S. policy and military circles of heavy strikes (including large ordnance) against Iranian targets, keeping escalation pressure high.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US reportedly considers use of "mother of all bombs"'; 'Trump says considering more military action against Iran.'

catalysts.title: Iran fortifies nuclear sites and rallies population
catalysts.description: Iran hardens key sites and mobilizes domestic support, signaling readiness for prolonged confrontation and deterrence posture adjustments.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran Fortifying Nuclear Sites and Rallying Its People for Return to Fighting.'

catalysts.title: Iran ships LPG/jet fuel despite U.S. blockade
catalysts.description: Continued Iranian fuel exports and ship movements that bypass blockade measures, sustaining supplies and signaling sanctions circumvention.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EXCLUSIVE: Iran ships some LPG, jet fuel despite US blockade, data shows.'

catalysts.title: Egypt seeks parliamentary backing to defend Saudi Arabia
catalysts.description: Egyptian leadership is pursuing formal parliamentary authority to support Saudi defense if requested, enabling potential regional military contributions.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked.'

catalysts.title: EU–Gulf summit postponed, delaying high-level diplomacy
catalysts.description: Postponement of scheduled EU–Gulf summit reduces immediate high‑level mediation opportunities and delays coordinated responses.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'EU and Gulf states postpone summit due in Saudi Arabia.'

catalysts.title: Airlines withdraw/relocate fleet and cut flights in region
catalysts.description: Airlines and event organisers pause operations and move aircraft out of the war zone, disrupting aviation and commercial connectivity.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Saudi Airlines Rush to Save Scores of Planes From a War Zone'; 'Airport attacks put aviation in crosshairs.'

catalysts.title: Further U.S./Western sanctions against Iran
catalysts.description: Additional rounds of sanctions and financial restrictions are likely as reprisal pressure increases, targeting Iranian entities and trade channels.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'US issues fresh Iran-related sanctions' and reporting of escalating policy responses.
